Dr. Jitendra Singh, Hon'ble Minister of Science & Technology, held a round table with biotech startups and investors at the launch BIO-NIVESH, a strategic platform connecting biotechnology innovators with investors to unlock private capital and accelerate the scale-up and commercialization of high-potential innovations.

The Minister said that innovation is incomplete without investment, and investment will not sustain itself without innovation. Government can take the initial risk, but private capital must build enterprises and take technologies to scale.

He suggested that the biotechnology ecosystem could adopt a "Big Five in Five Years" approach – building a few large anchor biotech companies under whose shadow other startups can grow.

India's bioeconomy has grown from USD 10 billion to over USD 195 billion, with more than 11,800 biotech startups. He stated that the next Industrial Revolution could be biotechnology driven and India must not be a late entrant.  

Government initiatives such as BioE3 and RDI, are building the enabling ecosystem that will take Indian biotechnology from innovation to impact at scale

Hon`ble Minster congratulated BIRAC for launching Bio-NIVESH that would help build the bridge required to take promising ideas from research and entrepreneurship to industry, scale and markets.

Sustain Plus | mach33

Up to 15% of food produced in India perishes due to lack of refrigeration. Medicines and vaccines also depend on consistent cooling from storage to delivery. Yet refrigeration remains unaffordable to many farmers and traders due to high upfront costs. Reefer trucks running on fossil fuels add to the ecological cost of this operation as well. Currently, there exists a gap of 3.2+ million metric tonne in India’s cold-chain capacity. 

Tan90 Thermal, one of the winners of Social Alpha’s Techtonic: Innovations in Clean Energy (Edition 3), has developed a low-cost, proprietary Phase Change Material-based portable cold storage solution, offered as cooling-as-a-service, to make farm-to-fork transportation more efficient and less carbon-intensive. 
Tan90 Thermal is an example of how hands-on mentorship, product development assistance, and catalytic funding can reimagine innovation in energy access and efficiency, especially in critical sectors like food and pharma.

Can cities become the farms of the future?

In this article, Dr. Arpit Shukla, Incubation Manager, VentureStudio Bio-NEST, explores the promise and limitations of urban farming.

From rooftops, basements, and warehouses to hydroponics, aeroponics, and controlled environment agriculture, urban farming is often presented as the future of food. But is it truly a scalable solution, or sometimes just a sustainability theatre?

Dr. Shukla offers a grounded perspective on where urban farming works, where it falls short, and why its real value may lie in climate-conscious, resource-efficient, and resilient city-building.
